seta elongated: A seta can be elongate.
tertiary leaf vein conspicuous: Tertiary veins can be conspicuous or distinct.
short shoot increased length: The examples (mentum, spur, 'longer than ovary') describe other parts. A short shoot is the wrong bearer here.
alar cell quadrangular: Alar cells (mosses) can be quadrate.
prolate: The text says ellipsoidal, which is the PATO ellipsoid. Prolate is a different, narrower term, so this is the wrong reading.
pubescent hair: A domatium can be pubescent. The examples are French and are correct.
banner petal spheroid: 'Appendices subglobuleux' describes appendages. The banner petal is the wrong bearer, so the pair exists only through a wrong part reading.
fruit ratio: A fruit has a length-to-width ratio.
spadix inflorescence subcylindrical: A spadix or its zone can be cylindric.
leaf bent: 'Angled' (an angle at the base or side) is not 'bent'. The PATO term means something else.
pappus ciliated: A pappus can be ciliate.
trichome characteristic: 'Characteristic' is too generic. 'Simple or forked' is a branching type. A rule or a specific trichome-type term is needed.
perigynium entire: A perigynium (beak margin) can be entire.
leaflet scaly: A leaflet can be scaly or lepidote.
petal optical quality: A petal has a colour. The PATO term is generic, so a more specific colour term is better where possible.
pappus increased thickness: A pappus can have stout or thickened bristles.
higher order inflorescence axis hairy: Inflorescence branches can be hairy.
pedicel dilated: A pedicel can be dilated at its tip.
leaf lamina tooth glandular: Teeth can be glandular.
bracteole has fewer parts of type: A count of bracteoles can be few. The examples are correct.
leaf apex subulate: A leaf apex can be subulate.
deciduous (generic): A spathe can be deciduous. The 'caducous' example is a close synonym.
leaf lamina low brightness: A leaf blade can be dark. 'Dark' is a colour tone.
portion of secretory tissue diameter: A secretory tissue portion (gland, resin spot) has a diameter.
stalk low brightness: A stipe or stalk can be dark.
convex: An orchid labellum can be convex. Some examples are about the midvein or an outer face, so check that the part is right.
plant cell inconspicuous: Leaf cells can be obscure or indistinct.
leaf rachis spiny: A leaf rachis can bear prickles, so it can be spiny.
funnel-shaped: A corolla tube can be funnel-shaped. The French examples are correct.
pistillate flower color: Pistillate flowers have a colour. The examples are correct.
leaf sheath increased size: Large or ample leaf sheaths. The size is meaningful.
panicle inflorescence color: Panicle colour is meaningful. Some examples describe the colour of the hairs (indument), which is still a colour of the panicle.
spore capsule operculum 2-D shape: The operculum (lid) has a 2-D shape such as ovate.
style brush-like shape: A penicillate (brush-like) style is a standard term.
capsule fruit obovate: Capsules can be obovate.
legume fruit attenuate: A legume can be attenuate at its ends.
secondary leaf vein orientation: Secondary veins can be ascending or spreading, which is orientation.
bud scale leaf shape: Bud scales have a shape. Some examples describe the apex or margin, so a rule should send those to the sub-part.
plant cell decreased size: Cells can be small. This is common in moss floras.
bud scale leaf spatial pattern: Valvate and imbricate describe how bud scales are arranged, which is a spatial pattern.
glabrous: Glabrous is meaningful for this part, for example a corona. The examples are correct.
leaf lamina tooth spreading: Teeth can be spreading.
bract increased width: Bracts can be wide. Comparative statements such as 'broader than' may need a separate rule.
nut fruit prolate: Ellipsoid is mapped to prolate. A nut can be ellipsoid.
glabrous: Glabrous is meaningful. The examples include surface qualifiers (adaxially), which are acceptable.
seed filiform: The examples describe hairlike appendages or papillae on the seed, not a filiform seed. This is a wrong reading, and the quality belongs to the appendage.
petal overlapping: Petals can overlap, as in an imbricate corolla.
leaf sheath red brown: Leaf sheaths can be chestnut brown, which is a red-brown colour.
bract velutinous: A velvety indument on bracts is common.
stamen non-deciduous (any body part): Stamens can be persistent.
leaf lamina lobe subcircular: Lobes can be subcircular.
plant ovary subcylindrical: An ovary can be subcylindrical.
palea winged: A palea can be winged. The keel wings are part of the palea.
leaflet straight: The examples say 'straight hairs', so the quality belongs to the trichome and not the leaflet. The part is wrong.
leaf apex cuspidate: A leaf apex can be cuspidate.
glandular: An indusium can be glandular. Some examples describe glands on the margin, which is fine.

continuous: An indusium can be continuous or interrupted.
ligule coriaceous: A ligule can be leathery (coriaceous).
connective decreased width: A connective can be narrow.
leaf sheath auricle inconspicuous: Auricles can be inconspicuous.
scale leaf non-deciduous (any body part): Scale leaves and cataphylls can be persistent.
whole plant disposition: The examples are about stinging hairs, so this is a wrong reading. The disposition (stinging) belongs to the trichome, not the whole plant.
receptacle decreased size: A receptacle can be small.
length: An androgynophore has a length.
capsule fruit actinomorphic: A capsule can be radially symmetric (actinomorphic).
leaf rachis hairy: A rachis can be hairy.

seed oblate: A seed can be oblate (depressed-globose).
plant ovary constricted: An ovary can be constricted, for example at its neck.
plant ovary punctate: An ovary can be punctate (gland-dotted).
auriculate: A pinnule can be auriculate.
trichome sessile (sensu botany): A trichome can be sessile.
flower odorless: A flower can be odorless.
length: Beak length is meaningful. One example is a distance from the beak tip, which is a measurement.
bract firm: A bract can be firm in texture.
sharpness: An apex can be acute or blunt, which is sharpness.
spike inflorescence prolate: A spike can be ellipsoid.
flower nocturnal: A flower can be nocturnal.
concave 3-D shape: An indusium can be horseshoe-shaped or pouch-forming, which is a concave shape.

position: Lobes can be erect, spreading or reflexed; position is meaningful for lobes.
orientation: Lobe orientation (ascending, spreading, divaricate) is correctly annotated.
achene fruit punctate: Achene surfaces are punctate or puncticulate (dotted).

spreading: Lobes and apices can be spreading. I judged this from the examples, because the part label is empty.
stamen vestigial: Rudimentary or vestigial stamens, for example in pistillate flowers, are standard.
texture: Texture such as membranous or papillose is meaningful for corona, margin and appendage parts. The part label is empty, so I judged this from the examples.
fleshy: Fleshy segments are normal. The part class is generic, so the examples carry the judgement.
plant spore rugose: Spore surfaces can be rugose or rugate (wrinkled).
sporophyll morphology: Sporophylls are described as monomorphic, homomorphic or dimorphic; morphology covers this.
leaf apex transparent: A hyaline or transparent leaf apex or hair-point is a normal description.
short shoot pilosity: The examples describe the spur of a petal (bearded) or general pubescence, not a short shoot. This looks like a wrong mapping of 'spur' to short shoot.
megasporophyll shape: Seed scales (megasporophylls) in cones are described by shape, such as reniform or flabellate.
leaf lamina adaxial epidermis hispidulous: Surface hairiness (hispidulous) on the adaxial leaf surface is correct.
pilosity: Subglabrous and glabrous are hairiness (pilosity) values for this surface or organ.
unstructured: Margins are described as subentire, which is a margin form close to entire.
lanceolate: Pinnules and similar parts can be lanceolate.
reflexed: Spathes and similar organs can be reflexed.
elliptic: A labellum can be elliptic.

triangular: Stelidia (orchid column projections) are triangular or deltoid.

erect: A rostellum can be erect.

tertiary leaf vein inconspicuous: Tertiary veins can be inconspicuous (obscure, indistinct).
secondary xylem hardness: Wood hardness (secondary xylem) is a standard wood-anatomy character.
strobilus terminal: A strobilus can be terminal on a branch or peduncle (a position).
shoot axis internode ciliated: Internodes can be ciliate.
peristome tooth height: Peristome teeth in mosses are measured by height in µm.
drupe fruit condensed: Wrong reading. 'Comprimée' means compressed or flattened (a shape). PATO condensed means something else (dense, packed). Use a compressed or flattened term.
panicle inflorescence 2-D shape: A panicle can be ovate or oval in outline.
curved: A perianth tube can be curved or arched (perianth tube = FLOPO_0986010).
leaf lamina tooth slender: Leaf teeth can be slender.
pedicel exserted: Pedicels can be exserted from a spathe, bracts or leaves.
peduncle hollow: Peduncles and scapes can be hollow (fistulose).
lenticel low saturation: Lenticels can be paler than the bark (a light colour).
pedicel falciform: Wrong reading. PATO falciform means sickle-shaped. 'Hooked' or 'uncinate' is a different shape, and the 'uncinate pubescent' row describes hairs, not the pedice
sepal optical quality: PATO optical quality is too general. 'Pale to deep blue' is a colour and belongs under the colour terms. The 'crisped pale hairs' row concerns hairs.
bract mealy: Bracts can be mealy or farinose (a surface covering of meal).
leaf sheath low saturation: A leaf sheath can be pale. 'Pale intervenal areas' belong to a sub-area, but the pair is fine.
flower deciduous (generic): Flowers can be deciduous or caducous.
reflexed: The orchid labellum or its apex can be reflexed.
leaf sheath entire: A sheath, mostly its margin, can be entire. The pair is meaningful.
non-deciduous (any body part): 'Persistent style base' is a normal character, with the base of the organ as the bearer.
trichome unbranched: Trichomes can be unbranched or branched.
leaf lamina adaxial epidermis floccose: The leaf adaxial surface can be floccose.
leaf sinus broad: A leaf sinus can be broad.
achene fruit sericeous: Achenes can be sericeous or silky. 'Silky-pubescent' is a close variant.
flower non-deciduous (any body part): Flowers or their parts can be persistent. The 'stylar column persistent' row concerns a sub-part, but the pair is fine.
thorn diameter: Thorns are measured by diameter.
seed subcylindrical: Seeds can be subcylindrical.
inflorescence bract obtuse: Bract apex or base shape (obtuse, rounded) is normal.
inflorescence bract lanceolate: Lanceolate bracts, including spatheoles, are common and the examples are correct.
short shoot ascending: The examples describe the angle of spurs, which are floral parts, not short shoots. The part is the wrong one.
cincinnus inflorescence present: Presence of cincinni (a kind of inflorescence) is a valid presence statement.
fruit subovoid: Subovoid fruits and capsules are correct.
style fimbriated: Fimbriate styles and stylar margins are correct.
corolla fringed: Fringed corolla margins or appendages are valid. Negated examples such as 'not fringed' must stay negated.
leaf isometrical: Isodiametric describes the cells of the leaf (bryophytes), not the leaf. The bearer should be the cell, and '1:1' is a ratio.
seed subtriangular: Subtriangular seeds are correct.
stamen deciduous (generic): Deciduous stamens are correct, and 'caduc' is the French equivalent.
plant ovary oblanceolate: Oblanceolate or oblanceoloid ovary outline is rare but meaningful.
scale leaf obtuse: Scale leaves and cataphylls can have obtuse apices.
flower nectary glabrous: Glabrous nectary discs and scales are correct.
leaf lamina adaxial epidermis scaly: Lepidote or scaly adaxial surface is correct.
mericarp papyraceous: Papery or chartaceous mericarps are correct.
present: Presence or absence of a crown or corona is a valid presence statement.
heart shaped: Cordate bases are normal for leaf-like parts and fern pinnae. Negated examples must stay negated.
samara fruit glabrous: Glabrous samaras are correct. 'Except' clauses need a partial-glabrous rule.
spikelet optical quality: 'Pale' and 'pallid' are colours. The generic optical quality is the wrong reading and should map to colour.
petal scaly: Lepidote or scaly-haired petals, usually on the outside, are valid.
scaphoid: Cymbiform or boat-shaped spathes and labella equal scaphoid.
scale leaf 2-D shape: The generic 2-D shape is valid for scale leaves, though the specific value (ovate) is better when available.
lanceolate-triangular: Triangular-lanceolate pinnae are a valid compound shape.
orbicular: Orbicular or suborbicular labellum is correct.
dilated: A dilated epichile is meaningful.
concave: A concave hypochile is correct.
plant ovary oblique orientation: An oblique ovary is a real orientation or symmetry feature.
leaf lamina abaxial epidermis setose: Setulose abaxial surface fits setose.
lemma decreased width: Narrow lemmas are correct.
shoot axis internode solid configuration: Solid internodes (not hollow) are correct.
semicircular: Semicircular leaf scars are correct.
leaf disposition: 'Stinging' describes the hairs, not a disposition of the leaf. The bearer should be the stinging hair, or the leaf needs a 'has stinging hairs' rule.
alar cell transparent: Hyaline alar cells are transparent.
costa convex: A convex costa, abaxially or adaxially, is correct.
paraphysis glandular: Glandular paraphyses or terminal cells are acceptable.
staminate flower pedicellate: Pedicellate staminate flowers are correct.
stipule velutinous: Velutinous stipules are correct, and 'velues' is a French equivalent.
spore capsule operculum texture: Texture of the operculum (membranous) is valid.
ligule decreased width: A narrow ligule is correct.
distance: Distance between phyllopodia is a valid spacing measure.
pendent: A pendent lip or spur is correct.
axillary hair color: Colour of axillary hairs is valid. Cell-level colour should be checked.
cortex amount: The number of cortex layers is a count, which fits amount.
drupe fruit oblong: Oblong drupes are correct.
panicle inflorescence pilosity: Indumentum of a panicle (pilosity) is valid.
leaf sheath filamentous: Leaf sheaths that break into fibres (filamentose) are correct. Negated examples must stay negated.
bulb spheroid: Subglobose bulbs are spheroid.
leaf lamina erose: An erose leaf margin is correct.
inflorescence continuous: Uninterrupted (continuous) inflorescences are correct. Negation, such as 'not interrupted', must be handled.
perichaetal bract size: Size of perichaetal bracts is valid, though the examples are comparative.
flower diurnal: Diurnal flowers are correct.
petal abaxial epidermis hairy: A hairy abaxial petal surface is correct.
spikelet orientation: Spikelet orientation (spreading, ascending) is correct.
filament winged: Winged filaments are correct.
capsule fruit linear: Linear capsules are normal (Brassicaceae siliques, Onagraceae and others).
portion of secretory tissue broad: A gland or secretory area can be broad. The examples are about glands, so the part mapping is a little loose.
costa transparent: The examples describe hyalocysts and a hyaline hairpoint, not the costa. This is a wrong part reading. A hyaline costa itself is rare.
spike inflorescence drooping: Spikes can droop or nod.
perigynium dentated: Perigynium beaks are toothed (bidentulate), so this is correct for sedges.
perigynium decreased thickness: Perigynium wall thickness (thin) is a real character in Carex.
thorn characteristic: PATO 'characteristic' is the root term and too generic. The examples are 'or' alternatives (stout or slender, erect or reflexed) that need specific terms.
spikelet prolate: Spikelets can be ellipsoid. Ellipsoid reads as prolate here.
inflorescence bract spatial pattern: 'Spatial pattern' is a generic parent. The examples mix imbricate (arrangement) and reticulate (surface pattern), so each needs its own specific term.
bark mealy: Mealy or farinose bark or surface is a real descriptor.
elliptic: Lobes and blades can be elliptic.
leaf sheath dilated: Leaf sheaths can be dilated.
stigma hemispheroid: Hemispheric stigmas are common.
receptacle non-deciduous (any body part): A persistent receptacle is a normal fruit character.
ridged: Discs and similar surfaces can have ridges.
bracteole fimbriated: Fimbriate margins on bracteoles are normal.
bract abaxial epidermis color: The bract surface can have a colour.
ray flower hairy: Ray flowers (corolla tubes) can be hairy.
filament terete: Filaments can be terete.
leaf margin setose: Leaf margins can be setose.
curved: Rostellum lobes can be curved.
shape: The viscidium has a shape. Shape is the attribute for the specific shape values.
pilosity: A surface can have a hair covering (pilosity) such as puberulent or glabrous.
color: A surface can have a colour.
receptacle hemispheroid: Hemispheric receptacles occur (for example in Asteraceae).
sporophyll glabrous: Sporophylls can be glabrous.
decreased width: Lobes, margins and bases can be narrow.
texture: Papillose is a surface texture.
leaf apex characteristic: 'Characteristic' is the generic root term. The examples are 'or' alternatives (caudate or acuminate) that need specific shape terms.
samara fruit color: Samaras have colours.
leaf lamina abaxial epidermis hispidulous: The abaxial epidermis can be hispidulous.
pubescent hair: Pubescent hair cover is normal for plant surfaces.
fruit multi-colored: Fruits (achenes) can be variegated or multi-coloured.
leaf semicircular: Semiorbicular leaf shape is a normal term, though some examples refer to the base or leaf scars.
anther square: Anthers can be square in outline.
branch herbaceous: Branches can be herbaceous.
leaf fimbriated: Leaf margins and apices can be fimbriate.
leaf midvein broad: A midvein can be broad.
tertiary leaf vein parallelodromous: Parallelodromous is a venation pattern of the whole leaf. The examples say the tertiary veins run parallel to each other, which is a different meaning.
awn reflexed: Awns can be reflexed.
amount: '1-3 cm apart' is the spacing between pseudobulbs, not an amount. This is a wrong reading, and a spacing rule is needed.
short shoot sigmoid: The examples describe a spur (an orchid or flower spur) that was mapped to short shoot. This is a wrong part reading.
leaf lamina lobe pointed: Lobes can be pointed.
non-deciduous (any body part): A persistent stylopodium is normal in Apiaceae. There is only one flora, so it is less certain.
staminode texture: Staminodes can be papillate.
glume decreased size: Glumes can be small.
leaf sheath flattened: Leaf sheaths can be flattened.
leaf sinus width: Sinuses have a width.
pubescent hair: Pubescent hair cover is normal for tubes and surfaces.
flower nectary linear: Nectar scales can be linear.
scale leaf position: Cataphylls have a position (basal, remote).
ovate: Traps (bladders) can be ovoid, and ovate is the closest PATO term.
receptacle depth: A receptacle can have a depth (a concave receptacle).
color: An endostome has a colour.
flat: A syconium ostiole can be flat (plat, plan, plane). The examples are correct.
stem base purplish red: The base of a stem can be purplish red or tinged purplish red.
perigynium granular: Perigynium surface texture (granular) is normal in Carex descriptions.
erect: Perianth lobes can be erect or spreading. The examples are correct.
samara fruit elliptic: The shape of a samara can be elliptic.
stolon filiform: Stolons are described as filiform or threadlike.
alar cell increased size: Enlarged alar cells are a standard moss character.

leaf margin notched: A leaf margin can be notched. The examples are correct.
trichome slender: Trichomes and hairs can be slender.
entire: A leaflet lamina has an entire margin. 'Margins entire' in the examples is attributed to the lamina.
achene fruit constricted: Achenes or their apex can be constricted. Negated cases ('not constricted') are handled by negation.
perigynium sharpness: The examples are 'apex acute' and 'base acute'. They describe the shape of the perigynium apex or base, which is a normal Carex character.
leaf sheath hispidulous: Grass and sedge leaf sheaths are described as hispidulous.
involucral bract glutinous: Involucral bracts can be glutinous (sticky). Some examples describe a ridge rather than the bract, but the bract can have the quality.
short shoot spherical: Wrong part: 'apex globose' and 'spur pendulous, globose' describe an apex or a floral spur, not a short shoot. A short shoot is rarely described by 3-D shape.

leaf sheath sharpness: The sheath apex can be acute or acuminate. The shape is attributed to the sheath through its apex.
shape: Stipule lobes have a shape (triangular, lanceolate, linear). The examples are correct.
leaf base oblique orientation: An oblique leaf base is a standard character.
achene fruit warty: Achene surface can be verrucose (warty).
corolla orientation: Corolla lobes or limb can be spreading, ascending or erect. The orientation is read at the corolla level.
triangular: Corolla plicae can be triangular.
color: The staminal tube can be coloured. The colour values (yellow, pink, maroon) are correct.
plant ovary quadrangular: An ovary can be 4-angled or tetragonous (quadrangular in cross-section).
cup-shaped: A corona can be cup-shaped. The examples are correct.
rhomboid: A corolla lip can be rhombic or rhomboid.
stem fasciculated: Stems can be fascicled, meaning several stems arise together. Negated cases are handled by negation.
leaflet herbaceous: Leaflets can be herbaceous (soft, non-leathery texture), a standard fern and legume character.
stipule inflated: Stipules can be inflated at the base.
nectary ring shaped: A nectary can be annular (ring-like).
nectary quadrangular: Nectar scales (nectaries) can be quadrate, subsquare or quadrangular. The examples are correct.
papilla cell increased size: Papilla cells can be large. The examples are correct.
plant ovary angular: An ovary can be angular or angulate in cross-section.
undulate: Labellum lobes and their margins can be undulate. The examples are correct.
decreased length: A corolla lip can be short or shorter than petals or sepals.
palea decreased size: A palea can be small.
perianth spotted: A perianth can be spotted or speckled. The examples are correct.
conical: A spadix appendix can be conic.
acuminate: A spathe limb can be acuminate, with an acumen or tail.
strap-shaped: A rostellum or its arms can be tongue-like, ligulate or tape-like.
2-D shape: A rostellum can be ovate or ovate-triangular. The 2-D shape attribute is correct.
firm: An indusium can be firm (texture).
leaf lamina base auriculate: A leaf lamina base can be auriculate. Negated cases are handled by negation.
decreased size: A pseudobulb can be small or minute.
stigma decreased width: A stigma or its lobes can be narrow. Comparisons ('narrower than style') are a different pattern from the plain quality.
nut fruit constricted: A nut can be constricted. The examples refer to its angles, but the nut has the quality.
utricle capsule fruit oblong: A utricle can be oblong, including compound forms such as ovate-oblong.
tepal closed: Tepals can stay closed at anthesis or in fruit.
leaf base concave: A leaf base can be concave. The examples are correct.
peristome tooth undivided: Peristome teeth can be undivided. This is a standard moss character.
spore capsule calyptra increased size: A calyptra can be large.
prominent: A floral disc can be elevated or prominent.
leaf actinodromous: Palmately nerved leaves have actinodromous venation, so the pair is meaningful and the examples fit.
radicle decreased length: A short radicle is a normal embryo description.
decumbent: The FLOPO bearer is a pinna. Decumbent pinnae (lying down, tips rising) are meaningful in ferns and cycads.
leaf biennial life span: Wrong reading. 'Biennial' here means the leaf lives two years (leaf longevity). PATO 'biennial life span' describes a whole plant's life cycle, not a leaf.
leaf lamina tooth pointed: Pointed teeth are a normal leaf-margin description.
short shoot flattened: Flattened spurs or short shoots occur, for example in Ginkgo and Cercidiphyllum.
keel-shaped: Wrong reading. 'Crête médiane' is a median ridge or crest on the pinna rachis, a surface feature, not a keel-shaped rachis.
portion of secretory tissue translucent: Translucent glands and secretory canals are standard, for example in Rutaceae and Myrtaceae.
pappus element fragile: Fragile pappus elements (bristles or scales) are a normal Asteraceae character.
gynoecium pyramidal: A pyramidal pistil is meaningful, for example in Ericaceae.
branch constricted: Branches constricted at the nodes are meaningful, for example in Poaceae and Polygonaceae.
decurrent: A spine shield (cactus areole base) can be decurrent. The examples with a length and the flowering eye fit.
leaf lamina tooth simple: Simple versus compound teeth is a real margin character ('dents simples').
filament spreading: Spreading filaments are a normal stamen orientation.
stamen winged: Winged stamens or filaments occur and the examples are correct.
stolon ascending: Ascending stolons are normal.
petiole pulvinus increased thickness: A pulvinus thicker than its petiole is a normal comparative statement.
convolute: A convolute spathe, with its margins rolled around each other, is meaningful.
surface feature shape: 'Surface feature shape' is the wrong generic attribute. Conduplicate means folded lengthwise, a fold state of the lobe, so it needs a fold or vernation value.
falciform: Falcate (sickle-shaped) corona lobes and appendages are typical of Apocynaceae.
fruit complete structure: Wrong bearer. 'Septum complete' describes the septum, not the fruit as a whole. The septum or false septum should be the bearer.
leaf abaxial epidermis texture: Surface texture of the abaxial epidermis (papillose, scabrous, dull) is meaningful.
inflorescence bract deciduous (generic): Deciduous or caducous bracts are normal.
rhizome orientation: Rhizome orientation (horizontal, erect, descending) is meaningful.
perigynium biconvex: Biconvex perigynia are a standard Carex character.
secondary xylem increased weight: Heavy wood is a standard wood-property statement.
nut fruit rugose: Rugose nutlets are normal, for example in Boraginaceae and Lamiaceae.
seed decreased length: Short seeds are meaningful. Some examples describe seed parts (cells, collar, tail), so the annotator needs the part-level bearer for those.
fruit scaphoid: Boat-shaped (scaphoid, cymbiform) follicles are meaningful and the examples are correct.
leaf lamina tripartite: A tripartite or trifid lamina is a standard leaf-division character.
leaf decreased depth: Wrong bearer. Depth belongs to the sinus (or lobe), not the leaf. 'Sinuses shallow' should have the sinus as bearer, or lobing should be a leaf value.
involucral bract setose: Setose involucral bracts are meaningful.
fimbriated: Fimbriate infrastaminal scales are meaningful.
ray flower oblong: Oblong ray flowers (or their laminae) are normal.
decreased width: A narrow floral disc is meaningful. 'Disc narrow at top' may be a different disc, but the pair is fine.
alar cell shape: Cell shape of moss alar cells (quadrate, rectangular) is meaningful.
pedicel increased size: An enlarged pedicel, especially in fruit, is meaningful.
follicle fruit glabrous: Glabrous follicles are normal.
bud scale leaf tomentose: Tomentose bud scales are meaningful.
leaf lamina brittle: A brittle lamina is a normal texture statement.
paraphysis increased length: Paraphyses longer than the sporangia is a normal comparative in ferns.
linear: Linear stigma lobes or rays are meaningful.
leaf lamina vein structure: 'Structure' is far too generic. 'Coalesced 1–2 cm' means the veins are fused for a length, so it needs a fusion value and a length, not this attribute.
branch glaucous: Pruinose (waxy-bloomed) branches match glaucous and are meaningful.
palea decreased width: A narrow palea is a normal grass character.
linear: Wrong bearer. 'Disk glands linear' and 'disk scales linear' describe the glands or scales on the disc, not the disc itself.
characteristic: 'Characteristic' is a meaningless root attribute. The examples are 'X or Y' alternatives that the annotator split from other qualities, and the bearer is unclea
spotted: Spotted orchid labella are standard.
obtuse: An obtuse or rounded spadix appendix apex is meaningful in Araceae.
truncated: A truncate spadix appendix is meaningful.
shape: The stylopodium shape (conic, flat, depressed) is a standard Apiaceae character.
root sparse: Sparse roots or rootlets are a meaningful density statement.
erect: An erect spadix appendix is meaningful.
glume spiny: Spiny or spinulose glume keels and veins are meaningful in grasses.

branch fragile: Delicate or fragile branches are a normal description.
characteristic: Root term 'characteristic' with 'A or B' lists (herbaceous or papery, simple or pinnate). The pair carries no information.
leaf sheath auricle wrinkled: Wrinkled auricles are correctly annotated.
ligule convex: A convex ligule is correctly annotated.
lodicule obovate: Obovate lodicules (squamellae) are correctly annotated.
glistening: Shiny or lustrous surfaces occur on many parts (for example pseudobulbs). The examples match 'glistening'.
increased size: A large rostellum is a normal description of size.

utricle capsule fruit emarginate: An emarginate orifice or apex of a utricle is valid. The pair is meaningful, though the examples name the orifice.
utricle capsule fruit hispidulous: Hispidulous fruit surface (hairs) is a normal description.
length: Length with a measured value applies to any part.
dissected: A divided frond or blade (pectinately divided to the costa) is valid. A few examples are negated.
papilla cell present: The examples count papillae borne on the cell ('apex with 4 papillae'). That is a part count of another part, not a presence quality of the papilla cell itself.
spiny: An echinate or aculeate perispore is spiny, so this fits.
lamina increased thickness: A thick or thickened lamina is correctly annotated.
lateral leaf vein flat: Flat lateral veins (not raised or sunken) are valid.
spatial pattern: Mixed readings: reticulate venation, glandular punctation and valvate aestivation. 'Spatial pattern' is too generic for them.
peristome tooth cleft: Cleft peristome teeth are valid.
areole bud decreased size: Small areoles are correctly annotated.
capsule fruit condensed: PATO 'condensed' means something else. 'Compressed' (flattened) capsules need a flattened or compressed shape term.
legume fruit velutinous: A velvety (velutinous) legume is valid.
gemma texture: Papillose gemmae are a surface texture. The specific papillate value is better if it exists, but the attribute is fine.
paraphyllium branched: Branched paraphyllia are valid in bryophytes.
capsule fruit trilobed: Trilobed capsules are correctly annotated.
staminate flower position: Axillary position of staminate flowers is valid.
hypanthium oblique orientation: An oblique hypanthium is valid.
sigmoid: Sigmoid is correct for curved structures.
leaf lamina vein recurrent: Recurrent veins or veinlets are valid in fern venation.
spore capsule mouth 2-D shape: An ovate spore capsule mouth is valid.
increased length: Long, with a measured length, applies to any part.
whole plant bristly: A bristly plant (indumentum) is a common description.
leaf lamina lobe revolute: Revolute margins of lobes are valid. The quality really belongs to the margin, but the pair is meaningful.
funnel-shaped: A funnelform tube (perianth tube) is correctly annotated.
leaf filamentous: 'Filiferous' means bearing threads, not being thread-like. It is a wrong reading of 'filamentous'.
branch has fewer parts of type: 'Branches few' counts the branches. The count belongs to the parent, as in the counted-parts rule, not to the branch.
receptacle foveate: A pitted receptacle is correctly annotated.
whole plant hispidulous: Hispidulous plant vestiture is valid.
sepal base concave 3-D shape: A saccate sepal base is a pouch, which is concave. This is valid.
leaf lamina cup-shaped: A cupped lamina is valid.
spadix inflorescence increased length: A long spadix is valid. 'Longer than spathe' is a comparison, which is also fine.
fruit prism shaped: Prismatic fruits (cypselae) are valid.
flattened: Flattened parts, including dorsally or laterally flattened, are valid.
cuneate: A cuneate base is a standard term.
perigynium elliptic: An elliptic perigynium is correct.
shoot system height: Shoot height or length is valid.
trichome low saturation: Pale hairs mean low colour saturation. This is acceptable.
pollen sac color: Pollen sac colour is correctly annotated.
involucre subcylindrical: A subcylindric involucre is correct.
involucre ciliated: Ciliate involucre margins are valid.
length: Length with a measured value applies to any part.
spine leaf color: Spine colour is correctly annotated.
foveate: Pitted sides are valid, as in seeds or fruits.

capitulum inflorescence cylindrical: Heads and capitula are described as cylindric.
obtuse: The examples are mostly 'rounded' or 'rounded-discoid', which is not obtuse. The part is mixed (apex and disk).
seed cuboid: Seeds and achenes can be cubic.
mericarp foveate: Mericarp sides can be pitted (foveate).
seed isometrical: Isodiametric describes the surface or testa cells, not the seed. The bearer is wrong. A rule should assign it to the cell.
amount: 'In 2 series' counts the rows of the corona's parts, not the corona itself. A counted-parts rule is needed.

constricted: A tube or mouth can be constricted.
shoot axis trichome ciliated: 'margin ciliate' describes the margin of an organ, not a trichome. A trichome is not itself ciliated.
filiform: Corona lobes or segments can be filiform or threadlike.
flat: Flat is a valid quality for apex and glands.
plant ovule horizontal: Ovule orientation can be horizontal.
tepal decreased width: Tepals can be narrow.
leaf lamina lobe decreased depth: Lobes can be shallow.
pistillate inflorescence amount: The counts are of heads on branches or the rachis, not of the inflorescence. A counted-parts rule should handle this.
non-deciduous (any body part): Calyx lobes can be persistent.
pilosity: Indusia can be glabrous or hairy.
papyraceous: Papery texture is valid for this part.
leaf sheath soft: Leaf sheaths can be soft.
